transcript:
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Corva Coleman.
President Trump says he and U.S. and Iranian officials met for three hours yesterday on
the sidelines of the U.N. General Assembly in New York.
Trump called the meeting good.
This came after he delivered a speech to the U.N. saying he had to decide whether to make
a deal with Iran or annihilate the country.
Trump's ambassador to the U.N., Mike Waltz, says Trump was right to make the threat because
Iran only listens to strength.
I'm absolutely fine with it.
I think the American people are fine with it if ultimately we get to an agreement that
makes the next generation safe from an Iranian regime with a nuclear weapon.
He spoke to NPR's Morning Edition.
Stocks opened lower this morning as President Trump prepares to welcome Chinese leader Xi
Jinping to Washington.
NPR's Scott Horsley reports the Dow Jones industrial average slid about 130 points in
early trading.
Xi flies into the Washington area this evening and President Trump plans to be at the airport
to welcome him.
Leaders of the world's two biggest economies will discuss trade, technology and geopolitics
during their summit this week.
Canada's prime minister says his country's trade talks with India are making good progress.
Canada is working to beef up alternative trading markets in response to commercial tensions
with the United States.
And DoorDash has agreed to pay $131 million to settle claims that it underpaid delivery
drivers in New York City.
It's the largest worker settlement in the city's history.
DoorDash has also agreed to new monitoring after admitting, quote, "We screwed up."
Scott Horsley, NPR News, Washington.
A federal judge holds a hearing today on three media organizations' lawsuit against the federal
government.
CNN, MSNow and Politico want to overturn President Trump's ban on their reporting from the White
House.
They say it is a blatant violation of the First Amendment.
The former head of the U.S. Forest Service under the first Trump administration is speaking
out against a controversial reorganization of the agency happening under the current
administration.
NPR's Kirk Sigler reports former staffers argue the plan will dismantle the country's
primary wildfire agency.
The Forest Service, along with its parent agency, the U.S. Agriculture Department, are
undergoing a massive reorganization, including the closure of seven regional offices, research
stations, and the relocation of its headquarters from Washington, D.C., to Utah.
Vicki Christensen was a Trump appointee who ran the agency from 2018 to 2021.
The reduction in the federal workforce without any real specific strategy is concerning.
In a press call organized by environmental groups, Christensen said the broader reorg
of the Forest Service is misguided and lacking any accountability from Congress.
The USDA has defended it in statements to NPR saying it will make the agency more efficient.
Kirk Sigler, NPR News.
You're listening to NPR News from Washington.
Reports from northern Ethiopia say Tigrayan fighters have seized the main airport in the
region.
The main airline there says flights have been canceled but did not say why.
Tigray's regional government says its forces have started a defensive war against Ethiopian
federal troops.
This comes after seven Ethiopian rebel groups joined in an alliance to challenge the federal
government.
The African Union estimates previous fighting between Tigrayan rebels and federal Ethiopian
troops left some 600,000 people dead.
In the U.S., social media influencer Braden Peters has been accused of rape.
A 17-year-old girl accused the man who uses the online name Clavicular and bears Chloe
Veltman reports Peters has denied the allegations.
20-year-old Braden Peters is known for looks-maxing, a digital subculture focused on maximizing
male physical appearance.
According to court records filed in Massachusetts, the teenager began communicating with Peters
on Instagram, where he paid her to appear on his livestreams to help increase her profile
on social media.
Peters then arranged for the minor to come to his home, where, on May 23, she alleges
he got her drunk on vodka and had sex with her without her consent.
NPR does not name alleged victims of sexual assault.
Peters will be arraigned next month on charges of rape, drugging a person for sexual intercourse
and procuring and providing liquor to a person under 21.
Chloe Veltman, NPR News.
On Wall Street, the Dow is now down 150 points.
I'm Corva Coleman, NPR News in Washington.
This weekend, up first, we talk about the economy.
Trucks, trains, and tractors run on diesel, which is now priced at record highs, with
less than 50 days until the midterm elections.
So the next six weeks are going to be intense.
Let Up First get you through it one morning at a time, with three stories you need to
know each day.
Listen to Up First on the NPR app or wherever you get your podcasts.

topics.text: President Trump says he and Iranian officials met for three hours at UN General Assembly
Stocks open lower as President Trump prepares to welcome Chinese leader Xi Jinping to Washington
Canadian Prime Minister says trade talks with India making good progress amid US tensions
DoorDash agrees to pay $131 million to settle underpayment claims for New York City delivery drivers
Federal judge holds hearing on media organizations' lawsuit against Trump's ban on White House reporting
Former Forest Service head criticizes controversial reorganization of agency under current administration
Tigrayan fighters seize main airport in northern Ethiopia amid renewed conflict with federal troops
Social media influencer Braden Peters accused of rape by 17-year-old girl in Massachusetts
